mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 2% YoY signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPIAUCSL YoY > 2% does not correlate with subsequent tightening actions by the Fed.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% signals a tightening labor market, which leads to wage inflation and increased production costs, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or UNRATE < 4% does not correlate with subsequent wage inflation.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) signals strong consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in periods of RSAFS growth are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% MoM signals a contraction in supply, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days due to reduced economic activity.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or INDPRO MoM < -1% does not correlate with subsequent economic slowdown.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the CPI (CPIAUCSL) is rising, the combination signals aggressive monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the combination of FEDFUNDS > 4% and rising CPIAUCSL does not correlate with subsequent tightening actions by the Fed.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) rises above 6% and payroll employment (PAYEMS) declines, the combination signals a weakening labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the combination of UNRATE > 6% and declining PAYEMS does not correlate with subsequent economic slowdown.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) signals strong demand in the housing market, which boosts related sectors and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 5-day forward returns in periods of HOUST growth are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When GDP (GDPC1) growth slows to less than 1% YoY and industrial production (INDPRO) is flat or declining, the combination signals a supply-side slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the combination of GDPC1 YoY < 1% and flat/declining INDPRO does not correlate with subsequent economic slowdown.
